findings.title: Affine rescaling does not biject the fixed canonical center lattices

claims: Lemma 3.3 second assertion and last proof paragraph

counterexample.assumptions: All scales strictly negative dyadic powers; all required triples admissible; outer and inner centers on specified grids and in Omega.
counterexample.stated_result: All target lattice coordinate ratios are integers.
counterexample.actual_result: Middle ratio is 1/1024, not an integer.

findings.counterevidence: Exact metric isometry is verified and remains true; later covering relations allow constant factors.
findings.impact: Invalid fixed-grid transport in the rescaling derivation used by Lemma3.11 and limiting branching-function blow-ups; local bounded-factor repair verified, principal incidence exponents not refuted.

repair.statement: Retain isometry; replace fixed-grid bijection by uniform comparability of canonical and pulled-back covers.
repair.verified: Bounded-overlap, common-volume and bounded-intersection analytic argument in report.
repair.remaining: Audit propagation through uniformity and all later lemmas.

independent_acceptance_check.reason: Outer/inner dyadic scales and centers satisfy the actual definitions; inverse-center lattice ratios are exactly (1,1/1024,2). The metric isometry survives but the stated grid and rectangle bijections fail. Rescaling canonical counts is used to transfer Lemma3.7 to X' in Lemma3.11 and establish blow-up closure of branching functions. Equal-volume, bounded-overlap covers plus approximate metric transitivity give the stated weaker comparison. This repairs the local step, not every downstream use, and does not lower an invalid core transport derivation to Minor.
